resources.string: Per-device steps for BT / wired / speaker · steps 10–100 · key segments 10–29
Customize media volume steps (10–100) and volume-key increments (10–29), with Bluetooth absolute / relative / default volume modes and the real system curve view.
Customize media volume steps (10–100) and volume-key increments (10–29), with two volume control modes.
When off, every device falls back to the system default volume

10–100 steps are allowed (default is the system native count). More steps mean a finer volume bar with more distinguishable levels. Changes stay in the UI until you tap Save, then follow the restart prompt.

Each volume-key press jumps about “steps ÷ segments” levels. More segments mean smaller jumps; the on-screen slider is not limited and can be tuned one step at a time. When disabled or reset, segments default to the phone’s default step count.

The tabs above switch between Bluetooth / wired headset / speaker, each keeping its own mode and range. Bluetooth offers absolute / relative / default; speaker and wired offer only relative / default (absolute volume is Bluetooth-only). Absolute: Bluetooth maps through AVRCP. Relative: the phone attenuates with a software curve. Default: the device linearly remaps system steps within the chosen range and keeps the native curve. With the master switch off every device is passthrough.
Choose how steps distribute across the volume range; in all three, step 1 = minimum and the top step = maximum. Curves for absolute and relative mode are stored separately.

1. Enable this module in LSPosed, then restart the system framework (the button on the home page does it).
2. Media volume steps: 10–100 (HyperOS ships 15 natively). A step is one distinguishable position on the volume bar and only affects the media stream; after changing steps tap “Restart system framework” — a short black screen is normal. The volume-key increment (10–29 segments) sets how many steps one press skips (about steps ÷ segments) and affects only the keys, not the on-screen slider.
3. Absolute mode: Bluetooth keeps absolute mapping (steps map through the curve to AVRCP 0–127); step 1 = minimum, top step = maximum.
4. Relative mode (best fix for quiet low volume): absolute volume is disabled and the phone attenuates the signal with a software curve while the headset stays at its own hardware volume.
5. Default mode: the step count is untouched and no custom curve is added — system steps are split linearly inside the chosen min/max, both ends anchor to min/max and the middle keeps the ROM native loudness curve (full range = passthrough); switch the chart axis (dB linear / perceived loudness) to inspect that native curve.
6. The device tabs switch between Bluetooth / wired / speaker and each keeps its own mode and range (the app focuses the current output on launch). Absolute is Bluetooth-only; relative attenuates in the system for all three devices within their own range; default remaps that device’s steps linearly inside min/max keeping the ROM curve. The step count and key increment are global.
7. Applying: tap Save and confirm the restart prompt. Mode or range changes need “Restart Bluetooth”; step changes need “Restart system framework” (the key increment applies immediately).
8. Restore defaults: open Settings → Diagnostics → “Restore system default” to reset the configuration, then restart; you will be asked whether to clear what this app wrote. You can also disable the module in LSPosed and reboot.
9. Troubleshooting: check the status card for the effective step count, and open Settings → Diagnostics → Module log for the module’s own log.
